name: Kushan Empire
summary: A Central Asian empire on the Silk Road that helped spread Buddhism into China. It created Gandhara art, which mixed Greek and Indian styles.

knownFor.label: Gandhara Buddha statues
knownFor.note: Some of the first human images of the Buddha, mixing Greek and Indian styles.

knownFor.label: Kushan gold coins
knownFor.note: Gold coins showing Greek, Iranian, Indian and Buddhist gods.

location.value: Afghanistan, Pakistan, northern India and parts of Central Asia.
location.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

terrain.value: The Hindu Kush mountains, the Bactrian plains and the Indus and Ganges valleys.
terrain.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

climate.value: Varied: dry mountain valleys in Bactria, monsoon plains in northern India.
climate.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

resources.value: Farmland and control of trade routes between Rome, India and China.
resources.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

disasters.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

population.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

urbanisation.value: Capitals at Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura; cities such as Taxila and Begram.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

disease.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

migration.value: Descended from the Yuezhi, who migrated from the Chinese frontier.

economicBase.value: Trade between the Roman Empire and China, plus farming.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

tradeRoutes.value: The Silk Road and sea routes to the Roman Empire via Indian ports.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

moneyAndTax.value: Gold coins (Kushan dinara) modelled on Roman coins.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

inequality.value: A ruling Kushan elite above merchants, farmers and local rulers.
inequality.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

governmentType.value: Monarchy under an emperor, with satraps governing regions.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

keyRulers.value: Kujula Kadphises (founder), Vima Kadphises, Kanishka I (c. 127–151), Huvishka, Vasudeva I.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

succession.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

institutions.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

stability.value: About 200 years of relative peace, sometimes called the “Pax Kushana”.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

eliteConflict.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

armyAndTech.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

majorWars.value: Wars with the Han general Ban Chao (around 90 CE) and later the Sasanians.
majorWars.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Parthians, Sasanians and Han China.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

inventions.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

openness.value: Used Greek, then Bactrian; patronised Buddhism, Hinduism and Zoroastrianism.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

religion.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

languageWriting.value: Greek until about 127, then Bactrian; also Gandhari.

artsArchitecture.value: The Gandhara school of Buddhist art and the Mathura school.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

socialStructure.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

sharedIdentity.value: Kings who claimed divine status on their coins.
sharedIdentity.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

neighbours.value: Rome (trade), Han China, Parthia and the Sasanians.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

ideasReligions.value: Buddhism spread to Central Asia and China.

colonisation.source: Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

riseSignals.value: Kujula Kadphises united the Yuezhi tribes.

peakPeriod.value: Under Kanishka I (c. 127–151), from Central Asia to the Ganges plain.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Kushan Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Liu, The Silk Road in World History (2010)

declineSignals.value: Fragmented in the 3rd century and lost lands to the Sasanians.

outcome.value: Fell to the Sasanians, Guptas and Kidarites. End date 350 or 375.

sources.value: Coins, inscriptions, Chinese sources. Checked against Wikipedia (“Kushan Empire”).

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. Dates of kings are disputed.
